title: Pastoral Study Guide: Guarding the True Gospel (Galatians 1 & 1 Cor 15)
description: Printable Swahili & English sermon-prep study guide on the four pillars of the biblical gospel (God, Man, Christ, Response) and answering the prosperity distortion.
content_html:
Guarding the True Gospel in East African Pulpits

Key Scriptures: 1 Corinthians 15:1–4; Galatians 1:6–9; Romans 3:21–26; Ephesians 2:8–9.

Maandiko ya Msingi (Core Scriptural Summary)

The gospel (Injili) is not good advice about how to earn earthly blessing; it is the royal announcement of what God Himself has accomplished through the sinless life, substitutionary death, and bodily resurrection of Jesus Christ.

The Four Biblical Pillars of the Gospel

  1. Holy God (Mungu Mtakatifu): Creator and righteous Judge who made humanity to know, worship, and reflect His glory (Isaiah 6:3; Psalm 24:1).
  2. Sinful Humanity (Mwanadamu Mwenye Dhambi): All people have rebelled against God's righteous rule and stand rightly condemned under His wrath, unable to save themselves by tithes, offerings, or good deeds (Romans 3:23; Ephesians 2:1–3).
  3. Sufficient Christ (Kristo Anayetosha): The eternal Son of God became man, lived in perfect obedience, bore our sins as our substitute on the cross, and rose triumphantly on the third day (1 Peter 2:24; 2 Corinthians 5:21).
  4. Biblical Response (Toba na Imani): God commands all people everywhere to turn from sin and idols (repentance) and trust wholly in Christ alone for forgiveness and eternal life (Mark 1:15; Acts 17:30).

Testing Sermons Against Scripture

  • Does the message make Christ's cross central, or does it treat God as a tool for financial gain?
  • Are listeners called to humble repentance and joyful obedience, or promised guaranteed wealth for 'seed' money?
  • Does the passage's main point in context drive the sermon's main point?

Discussion Questions for Elders & Church Leaders

1. How can we shepherd congregation members who face genuine poverty without turning the pulpit into a prosperity transaction?
2. Which verses in Galatians 1 and Romans 3 should every member of our church memorize to recognize false teaching?

title: Elders & Deacons Handbook: Biblical Church Leadership (1 Tim 3 & Titus 1)
description: A practical printable handbook for East African pastors on raising plural elders, training deacons for mercy ministry, and practicing restorative church discipline.
content_html:
Biblical Leadership for a Healthy Local Church

Key Scriptures: 1 Timothy 3:1–13; Titus 1:5–9; 1 Peter 5:1–4; Acts 6:1–7; Matthew 18:15–17.

Christ Is the Chief Shepherd

The local church does not belong to its founding pastor—it was purchased with the precious blood of Christ (Acts 20:28). Pastors serve as under-shepherds accountable to the Chief Shepherd (1 Peter 5:4).

1. Qualifications of an Elder / Overseer (Mzee wa Kanisa)

  • Character First: Above reproach, faithful in marriage, sober-minded, self-controlled, hospitable, not violent, not a lover of money (1 Tim 3:2–3).
  • Household Faithfulness: Managing his own household well with gentleness and dignity (1 Tim 3:4–5).
  • Teaching Competence: Able to teach sound doctrine and gently rebuke those who contradict it (Titus 1:9).

2. Role of Deacons (Mashemasi)

Modeled in Acts 6:1–7, deacons protect church unity by caring for widows, practical needs, administration, and finances—freeing the elders to devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the Word.

3. Practical Steps for Your Church This Quarter

  1. Identify 2–3 faithful men already displaying 1 Timothy 3 character and invite them into a 6-month weekly study of Titus and 1 Peter.
  2. Establish transparent financial accountability with at least two godly deacons overseeing offerings and budgets.
  3. Teach the whole congregation what meaningful church membership means from 1 Corinthians 12.

title: Expository Sermon Preparation Worksheet (6-Step Weekly Guide)
description: Step-by-step weekly sermon preparation template from Monday text observation to Sunday proclamation—designed for busy bi-vocational and rural pastors.
content_html:
6-Step Expository Sermon Preparation Worksheet

Anchor Verse: "Preach the word; be ready in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort, with complete patience and teaching." — 2 Timothy 4:2

Monday — Prayer & Careful Observation

Read the passage aloud at least 5 times (in both English and Kiswahili if preaching bilingually). Write down repeated words, key verbs, contrasts (but, therefore, because), and questions the text raises.

Tuesday — Context & Structure

Read the chapter before and the chapter after. Outline the natural paragraphs or stanzas of the text. Never force a 3-point outline onto a text that only has 2 movements!

Wednesday — Melodic Line & Main Idea

Summarize what the biblical author was saying to the original audience in one clear sentence. This is the spine of your sermon.

Thursday — Connection to Christ & the Gospel

Ask: How does this passage point to our need for Christ, His saving work, or the Spirit-empowered life of faith? Avoid moralism ('try harder'); ground every command in God's grace.

Friday — Pastoral Application for Your Congregation

Apply the passage faithfully to real households in your church: husbands and wives, youth, grieving families, businesspeople, and unbelieving visitors.

Saturday — Prayerful Review & Clarity Check

Cut unnecessary illustrations that distract from Scripture. Pray for the Holy Spirit to open ears and soften hearts as the Word is proclaimed on Sunday.

title: Pastoral Visitation & Grief Care Guide (Biblical Comfort in Suffering)
description: Scripture-anchored guidance for hospital visits, bereavement counseling, family reconciliation, and guarding your own soul from pastoral burnout.
content_html:
Shepherding Through Grief, Illness & Hardship

Key Scriptures: Psalm 23; Psalm 34:18; 2 Corinthians 1:3–7; Romans 8:18–39; 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18.

Ministry of Presence

In deep sorrow, people rarely remember a long lecture, but they always remember a shepherd who wept with them (Romans 12:15), read God's promises quietly, and prayed with tenderness.

Hospital & Sickbed Visitation Checklist

  • Keep the visit brief (10–15 minutes) unless the family invites you to stay longer.
  • Listen first before speaking; ask how they are feeling and what they would like you to pray for.
  • Read one comforting, unhurried passage (e.g., Psalm 23, Psalm 121, or Isaiah 41:10).
  • Avoid blaming illness on 'lack of faith'—remember Job, Paul's thorn (2 Cor 12:7–9), and Timothy's frequent ailments (1 Tim 5:23).

Caring for Your Own Soul as a Pastor

Watch your life and doctrine closely (1 Tim 4:16). Guard one full Sabbath day of rest weekly, maintain a trusted brother pastor who can pray for you honestly, and nourish your own heart in Scripture daily—not only when preparing sermons.
